touches.text: Every verb anywhere is reached from the cairn command, as a path: cairn <device> [<machine> ...] <verb>. No central list: help at any level prints that level's own verbs under [<name>], alpha order, then calls back up the tree to its parent, which does the same, out to [cairn]. The groups come out flat, one after another, not nested: cairn codemother inspector_gadget help  -> [inspector_gadget] ... then [codemother] ... then [cairn] ... A device may ask another device help over the bus the same way; nothing being built needs that yet. (Q#2, Akien 2026-11-03)

The launcher walks the words. `cairn cairn foo bar` (the long form) means "tell the cairn device to run foo with argument bar". At each level: is the next word a machine here? Step into it and take the next word. Is it a script in this level's bin/? Run it, pass back the result, done. Neither? It is a bus verb: send it to this level over the bus. So `cairn foo bar baz`: foo is a device; it has a machine bar; bar's bin/ has baz, so baz runs. No bar machine? bar goes to foo over the bus. Each check is one directory lookup, so it is fast. (Q#12, Akien 2026-11-03)

Any device or machine may have a bin/ beside its code (cairn/devices/<device>/bin/, .../machines/<machine>/bin/). That folder IS its list of shortcuts: add a file to add one, delete it to remove one. A shortcut is just a script that calls the long form, which also saves the walk from searching farther (eg `cairn superclaude` → `cairn cc superclaude`; `cairn show temp` → `cairn recovery show temp`), or does work itself (eg initialization, install). Shortcuts can go anywhere, beside what they serve (RULE 1).
HISTORY: today it is bin/cairn dispatching to bin/cmd/<name>, 31 commands, most of which do the work themselves. Where each goes: 5.10.

Repo-root bin/ holds only the launcher itself (cairn, cairn.cmd), the one thing on PATH, so it runs even when the package won't import (5.3.2.7). Every shortcut lives in the bin/ of the device or machine it belongs to. Its bin/ plus its bus verbs is what help lists at that level (2.4.11). (Q#12: Akien let CC choose, 2026-11-03; CC kept his walk.)
Trouble tickets (3.3.3) live here. Any device has a direct line to raise one, not over the bus (2.2.8.1.3).

Two execution trees: at each segment, if there is a script for it in that device's bin, run it; otherwise go onto the bus and ask that device. Why: scripts are the simple path, and the bus is the operator's route to what a device answers itself, often faster (eg `cairn codemother show artifact <id>`). (Akien, 2026-11-05)

`cairn help` lists [all], then [operator], then [cairn], then every other device in alphabetical order, because `cairn` itself is special. Help is called, returns its results, and is done. Help at any other level looks in the bin folders inside that device's tree for the shortcuts relevant to the input. (Akien, 2026-11-05)
Trouble Device (cairn/devices/trouble/): → Recovery (7.3.4). Its store tool stays as the direct line (2.2.8.1.3).
